g1.label: 1. Point of view of the story
g1.why: The narrator uses 'I' throughout, so the story is told in the first person.

g2.correct: taking the unlocked bike for himself
accept: taking the unlocked bike for himself
g2.label: 2. What the narrator was seriously considering
g2.why: He notices the bike is unlocked and thinks nobody would know if he took it.

g3.correct: the narrator's inner conflict about what to do
accept: the narrator's inner conflict about what to do
g3.label: 3. What the clouds/storm mainly represent
g3.why: The clouds press lower as his temptation grows, and the storm breaks only once he decides.

g4.label: 4. What the narrator did when Felix asked about the bike
g4.why: He points at the fence and tells Felix the bike is there, safe.

g5.label: 5. What happens right after the narrator tells the truth
g5.why: The text says the first drops of rain broke through right after he pointed Felix to the bike.

g6.correct: the rain matches his sense of relief after doing the right thing
accept: the rain matches his sense of relief after doing the right thing
g6.label: 6. How the ending rain links to the narrator's feelings
g6.why: The narrator compares the rain breaking through to something inside him 'breaking open' — lighter and cleaner.

g1.label: 1. "I never told anyone what really happened that night."
g1.why: The narrator speaks as 'I', so this is first-person narration.

g2.label: 2. "Marcus stared at the letter, wondering if his father would ever forgive him."
g2.why: We only see Marcus's own thoughts from outside — that is third-person limited.

g3.label: 3. "Marcus felt sure he had been forgiven, but across town his father was already packing his bags."
g3.why: The narrator reveals what Marcus's father is doing elsewhere — something Marcus himself does not know — which only an omniscient narrator can show.

g4.label: 4. "I definitely wasn't scared — my hands were just cold, that's all."
g4.why: The narrator's defensive denial suggests they are not telling the whole truth — a sign of an unreliable narrator.

g5.label: 5. "We ran until our lungs burned, and even then I didn't dare look back."
g5.why: 'I' and 'we' mark the narrator speaking about their own experience: first person.

g6.label: 6. "Priya bit her lip, unsure whether to knock on the door."
g6.why: The narrator only shows us Priya's own uncertainty, from outside: third-person limited.

g7.label: 7. "Neither of them noticed the shadow slipping past the window behind them."
g7.why: The narrator describes something neither character notices — knowledge beyond any one character's view is a sign of an omniscient narrator.

g8.label: 8. "I only borrowed it — I was always going to give it back, I swear."
g8.why: The over-eager justification ('I swear') suggests the narrator is trying to convince us of something that may not be true.

g1.label: 1. The old oak tree
g1.why: A tree that survives every storm stands for the family enduring hard times.

g2.label: 2. The cracked watch
g2.why: Keeping a broken watch that no longer works represents refusing to let go of an earlier time.

g3.correct: her fear of making a big change
accept: her fear of making a big change
g3.label: 3. The gate at the end of the lane
g3.why: The gate only seems to grow taller when she thinks about leaving — it stands for how hard the decision feels, not its real height.

g4.correct: someone is waiting and holding on to hope
accept: someone is waiting and holding on to hope
g4.label: 4. The candle in the window
g4.why: A candle left burning after everyone else has gone to sleep is a classic image of someone waiting, still hopeful.

g5.label: 5. The closed bridge
g5.why: A bridge that connects two places being closed since an argument mirrors the broken connection between the people.

g6.correct: a sense of relief and a fresh start
accept: a sense of relief and a fresh start
g6.label: 6. The falling snow
g6.why: Snow falling at the exact moment she speaks her fear aloud suggests a clean, fresh start, not just weather.

g7.label: 7. The faded photograph
g7.why: A photograph fading until the faces can no longer be made out mirrors memories fading as time passes.

g8.label: 8 (review) — campaigners ___ for equal rights
g8.why: Review from 10g-slavery-civil-war: past perfect for an action completed before another past event ('by the time the law passed') — 'had fought'.
